reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates a dedicated hill session targeting climbing strength and threshold pace, which are crucial for trail running performance. Plan B, conversely, consists entirely of easy runs, lacking the specific stimulus needed to improve power and efficiency on varied terrain. While Plan B prioritizes recovery, Plan A’s structured approach, including a threshold hill workout, directly addresses the goal of increasing speed and trail-specific fitness. Furthermore, the inclusion of a longer hill session (40 minutes) provides a more substantial challenge than the extended easy run in Plan B.
